Gun Show License Plate Scans A Civil Rights Outrage, SAF Wants Probe

The trick here is that this is, in no way, illegal... Please read the whole post before flying off the handle!

The police can legally scan, and run, any plates that they can see, regardless of reason or if the vehicle is on private or public property. This is because you technically do not own your plates, but "rent" them from your state when you renew your tags every year. Even if you own your car, your plates MUST be in a visible spot, and those belong to the state. So, the actual scanning of plates isn't illegal, and is a really tricky way of looking for criminals.

The way this needs to be argued is via profiling. If the police try to impose any type of law enforcement, which results from these scans at a gun show, a good lawyer will say that their client was targeted via profiling, and get the entire thing dismissed. The police are targeting people, based on the fact that they're at a gun show, and that is exactly what profiling is... and to impose a ticket, arrest, or other form of law enforcement based on these scans, is tantamount to profiling.

Ultimately, I'd say that it would be a good thing for the police to "find" someone at one of these, write a ticket or make an arrest, and take it to court. If a good lawyer can get it thrown out for profiling, then a precedent can be set, and the police will stop doing this when they see that nothing can come of it, and it becomes a waste of time.

I'm not sure there is a solid basis to get any charges dismissed, actually. Profiling isn't illegal unless it is based on categories protected by law. While gun ownership is protected by the Second Amendment, gun owners are nt a protected class as would be the case if the profiling were based on race, religion, national origin, etc. There is no particular protection for people attending guns shows. It's no different than doing it at NFL games, music concerts, malls, etc. I mean I'd be willing to take the case and argue charges should be dismissed, but I wouldn't be shocked to lose, either.

You're correct, but not 100% right, and a jury-trial wouldn't necessarily depend on if gun ownership is a protected class, or not... not to mention that profiling isn't exclusively limited to protected classes. But, let's pretend that it is:

You'd just need to convince a jury that, if the government goes after legal gun shows like this, there's nothing to stop them from going to elementary/middle/high schools, during school plays or sporting events (completely legal functions), looking for "pedophiles" and running all of the plates of every car in the parking lot, writing tickets to any regular Joe for anything and everything... or there's nothing to stop the police from going to a grocery store under the guise of looking for "robbers" and running the plates of every shopper, arresting people while shopping...

If you convince the jury that profiling "shoppers" at a gun show is no different than profiling their grandmother for "shopping" at a grocery store, they'll protect their grandmother every time.

But the jury wouldn't have anything to do with it. It would be an issue of admissibility. Plus, there isn't even any profiling going on here. The cops are going to a public event and observing publicly displayed information. They aren't profiling anyone.

The arguments you mention would most likely be stopped short by the court if the prosecutor was doing his job. So you'd have a trial in which a guilty person is tried and the fact they were arrested because of a license plate scan at a gun show would be irrelevant.

I say all this as someone who thinks sending cops to do this at gun shows is a total waste of government resources. But the solution to that is to publicize the waste and elect people who won't waste our money. Saying cops cannot scan and run license plates in parking lots is not a good rule.
